chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the limit of the handshake, so he said: 'A circle of a palm tree'.
ai.seo_question: What is the defined limit or distance for a valid handshake in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise definition from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), grounding the etiquette of greeting in a tangible, natural measurement—the circumference of a palm tree—which reflects the practical jurisprudence of the early Shia community. This hadith not only delineates the physical scope of the handshake but also underscores the importance of modesty and clear boundaries in social interactions as emphasized in Shia fiqh. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how abstract legal limits were communicated through relatable, everyday objects in the prophetic tradition.
